newsitem.title: UK: Hormone therapy seen increasing cancer risk.
newsitem.headline: Hormone therapy seen increasing cancer risk.

text.p: Hormone replacement therapy in which women take oestrogen can increase the risk of cancer in the uterus, researchers said on Friday.
Women who take oestrogen after the menopause can reduce their risk of cardiovascular disease and osteoporosis.

But because oestrogen stimulates the growth of endometrial cells, which line the uterus, oestrogen replacement therapy can also increase the risk of endometrial cancer, according to Shirley Beresford of the University of Washington, Seattle, and colleagues.
To lower this risk, many women taking oestrogen are also given progestagen, which opposes the effects of oestrogen, for at least a few days a month.

Writing in the Lancet medical journal, the researchers said that compared with women who had never taken hormone replacement therapy for more than six months, women who took osterogens without progestagens had a four-fold increase in the risk of endometrial cancer.
In contrast, in women who took a progestagen with their oestrogen therapy there was little or no increase in the risk of endometrial cancer.
For women who took progestagen for 10 to 21 days each month, there was no significant increase in the risk of endometrial cancer.
But for those who took progestagens for fewer than 10 days a month, the risk was three times higher compared with non-users.
